es: Identificar la palabra base y el prefijo o sufijo en palabras como unhappy, kindness, careful, dishonest e impatient.

teaching.en: Mia looks unhappy today, but yesterday she was very happy.
teaching.es: Mia parece infeliz hoy, pero ayer estaba muy feliz.
teaching.explanationEs: Un- + happy = lo contrario: unhappy es «infeliz».
segments: Mia looks unhappy today, but
yesterday she was very happy.
teaching.audioText: Mia looks unhappy today, but yesterday she was very happy.

teaching.en: Thank you for your kindness; you are a very kind person.
teaching.es: Gracias por tu amabilidad; eres una persona muy amable.
teaching.explanationEs: El sufijo -ness convierte un adjetivo en sustantivo: kind → kindness.
segments: Thank you for your kindness; you
are a very kind person.
teaching.audioText: Thank you for your kindness; you are a very kind person.

teaching.en: Be careful with the glass, and take care of your little brother.
teaching.es: Ten cuidado con el vaso y cuida a tu hermano pequeño.
teaching.explanationEs: Care + -ful = careful: «lleno de cuidado», es decir, cuidadoso.
segments: Be careful with the glass, and
take care of your little brother.
teaching.audioText: Be careful with the glass, and take care of your little brother.

teaching.en: It is dishonest to copy a friend's homework, because honest students do their own work.
teaching.es: Es deshonesto copiar la tarea de un amigo, porque los alumnos honrados hacen su propio trabajo.
teaching.explanationEs: Dis- + honest = lo contrario: dishonest es «deshonesto».
segments: It is dishonest to copy a friend's homework,
because honest students do their own work.
teaching.audioText: It is dishonest to copy a friend's homework, because honest students do their own work.

teaching.en: Tom is impatient, but his sister is patient and waits for everyone.
teaching.es: Tom es impaciente, pero su hermana es paciente y espera a todos.
teaching.explanationEs: Im- aparece antes de p: im + patient. El prefijo cambia el significado.
segments: Tom is impatient, but his sister
is patient and waits for everyone.
teaching.audioText: Tom is impatient, but his sister is patient and waits for everyone.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada palabra derivada con su significado.

feedback.es: Cada palabra se entiende desde su base: un- niega, -ness forma el sustantivo y -ful indica «lleno de».

hint.es: Busca la base dentro de cada palabra: happy, kind y care.

prompt.es: ¿Qué significa unhappy en esta frase?

feedback.es: El prefijo un- da el sentido contrario: unhappy es «no feliz».

hint.es: El prefijo un- da el sentido contrario.

origin.text: Mia looks unhappy today.

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo contrario de happy es infeliz.»

feedback.es: Para el contrario de happy se añade el prefijo un-: unhappy.

hint.es: Añade a la base el prefijo que niega.

origin.text: The opposite of happy is ___.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ten cuidado con el vaso.»

feedback.es: Care + -ful forma careful, el adjetivo de «con cuidado».

origin.text: Be ___ with the glass.

prompt.es: Elige el sustantivo de kind para completar la frase.

feedback.es: Después de shows hace falta un sustantivo, no un adjetivo: kindness.

answer.text: It is dishonest to copy homework.

feedback.es: Dishonest es el adjetivo contrario de honest y va después de It is.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada palabra con su significado; fíjate en el prefijo.

feedback.es: El prefijo dis- o im- invierte el sentido de honest y patient.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige quién no espera con calma.

feedback.es: Impatient lleva el prefijo im-: Sara no espera con calma; Leo es patient.

feedback.es: Honest es la base; con el prefijo dis- pasaría a ser lo contrario.

origin.text: An ___ student never copies homework.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase usa bien el sustantivo kindness?

feedback.es: Kindness es un sustantivo: va tras your y no puede describir a una persona.

choices.text: He does not take things from other people.

feedback.es: Never takes anything that is not his significa que no toma lo ajeno: es honrado.

origin.audio: My cousin is careful with money, and he is honest. He never takes anything that is not his.

feedback.es: El contrario de patient lleva im- porque empieza por p: impatient.

origin.text: Tom never waits; he is very ___.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿por qué está triste Sara?

feedback.es: Dishonest significa no honrado, y eso es lo que entristece a Sara.

origin.text: Sara is unhappy because her friend is dishonest.

es: Formar sustantivos y adjetivos con -ness, -ity, -ful, -less, -able y los prefijos un-, dis- e im-.

teaching.en: Sara is very helpful; she helps everyone at the club.
teaching.es: Sara es muy servicial; ayuda a todos en el club.
teaching.explanationEs: Help + -ful = lleno de ayuda: servicial.
segments: Sara is very helpful; she
helps everyone at the club.
teaching.audioText: Sara is very helpful; she helps everyone at the club.

teaching.en: The lost dog looked helpless and sad.
teaching.es: El perro perdido parecía indefenso y triste.
teaching.explanationEs: Help + -less = sin ayuda: indefenso.
segments: The lost dog looked
helpless and sad.
teaching.audioText: The lost dog looked helpless and sad.

teaching.en: Her sadness disappeared when her friends arrived.
teaching.es: Su tristeza desapareció cuando llegaron sus amigos.
teaching.explanationEs: Sad + -ness = sustantivo: sadness.
segments: Her sadness disappeared when
her friends arrived.
teaching.audioText: Her sadness disappeared when her friends arrived.

teaching.en: Tom is reliable, but his cousin is unreliable and often forgets.
teaching.es: Tom es fiable, pero su primo es poco fiable y a menudo olvida cosas.
teaching.explanationEs: Un- + reliable = lo contrario. Reliable = rely + -able: «en quien se puede confiar».
segments: Tom is reliable, but his cousin
is unreliable and often forgets.
teaching.audioText: Tom is reliable, but his cousin is unreliable and often forgets.

teaching.en: It is impolite to arrive late, but polite people always say sorry.
teaching.es: Es descortés llegar tarde, pero las personas educadas siempre piden perdón.
teaching.explanationEs: Im- + polite = lo contrario; im- va antes de p.
segments: It is impolite to arrive late,
but polite people always say sorry.
teaching.audioText: It is impolite to arrive late, but polite people always say sorry.

teaching.en: Mia has a lot of creativity; she is creative with paper and colours.
teaching.es: Mia tiene mucha creatividad; es creativa con el papel y los colores.
teaching.explanationEs: Creative (adjetivo) → creativity (sustantivo con -ity).
segments: Mia has a lot of creativity; she
is creative with paper and colours.
teaching.audioText: Mia has a lot of creativity; she is creative with paper and colours.

hint.es: Necesitas un sustantivo: el sufijo termina en -ity.

feedback.es: El contrario de polite lleva im-: impolite.

feedback.es: Unreliable niega reliable con un-, y after a lot of necesitas el sustantivo creativity.

sentences: Tom does not keep his promise; he is ___ (reliable).

choices.text: She is nice to people and ready to help.

feedback.es: Polite y helpful indican que es amable con los demás y dispuesta a ayudar.

feedback.es: Si olvida los planes y llega tarde cada día, no se puede confiar en él: unreliable.

Tom is reliable and very helpful.

prompt.es: ¿Qué palabra tiene el sufijo que significa «sin»?

feedback.es: El sufijo -less significa «sin»: helpless es «sin ayuda».

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina el hablante de Tom.

choices.text: Tom is not nice when he asks for things.

feedback.es: Nunca dice please ni thank you: es impolite, descortés.

feedback.es: Después de be y very va un adjetivo: creative.

es: Deducir el significado de una palabra nueva a partir de su base conocida, su afijo y el contexto.

teaching.en: My old phone is useless; it never works.
teaching.es: Mi teléfono viejo es inútil; nunca funciona.
teaching.explanationEs: Use + -less = sin utilidad. El contexto (it never works) lo confirma.
segments: My old phone is
useless; it never works.
teaching.audioText: My old phone is useless; it never works.

teaching.en: Tom is forgetful: he often forgets his keys.
teaching.es: Tom es olvidadizo: a menudo olvida sus llaves.
teaching.explanationEs: Forget + -ful = que tiende a olvidar. El contexto lo confirma.
segments: Tom is forgetful: he
often forgets his keys.
teaching.audioText: Tom is forgetful: he often forgets his keys.

teaching.en: The picnic was enjoyable, and everyone had fun.
teaching.es: El picnic fue agradable y todos se divirtieron.
teaching.explanationEs: Enjoy + -able = que se puede disfrutar: agradable.
segments: The picnic was enjoyable,
and everyone had fun.
teaching.audioText: The picnic was enjoyable, and everyone had fun.

teaching.en: The new neighbour is unfriendly; she never says hello.
teaching.es: La vecina nueva es antipática; nunca saluda.
teaching.explanationEs: Un- + friendly = no amistoso: antipático.
segments: The new neighbour is unfriendly;
she never says hello.
teaching.audioText: The new neighbour is unfriendly; she never says hello.

teaching.en: Tom was careless and broke a window.
teaching.es: Tom fue descuidado y rompió una ventana.
teaching.explanationEs: Care + -less = sin cuidado: descuidado.
segments: Tom was careless and
broke a window.
teaching.audioText: Tom was careless and broke a window.

teaching.en: Sara is hopeful about the test, and Leo is thoughtful because he brings her a drink.

is thoughtful because he brings her a drink.
teaching.audioText: Sara is hopeful about the test, and Leo is thoughtful because he brings her a drink.

feedback.es: Use + -less significa sin utilidad, y el contexto (never works) lo confirma.

hint.es: Separa la base use del sufijo -less.

feedback.es: Hope + -ful significa con esperanza: hopeful.

es: Describir el carácter de una persona con adjetivos y sustantivos derivados apoyados en ejemplos de su conducta.

teaching.en: My cousin Rosa is generous: she shares her lunch with everyone, and her generosity makes us smile.
teaching.es: Mi prima Rosa es generosa: comparte su almuerzo con todos y su generosidad nos hace sonreír.
teaching.explanationEs: Generous → generosity. Un adjetivo de carácter + un hecho que lo demuestra.
segments: My cousin Rosa is generous: she shares her lunch
with everyone, and her generosity makes us smile.
teaching.audioText: My cousin Rosa is generous: she shares her lunch with everyone, and her generosity makes us smile.

teaching.en: Leo is brave; his bravery helped him speak in front of the class.
teaching.es: Leo es valiente; su valentía le ayudó a hablar delante de la clase.
teaching.explanationEs: Brave → bravery: del adjetivo al sustantivo cambia el final.
segments: Leo is brave; his bravery helped him
speak in front of the class.
teaching.audioText: Leo is brave; his bravery helped him speak in front of the class.

teaching.en: Mia is shy at first, but her shyness disappears when she knows you.
teaching.es: Mia es tímida al principio, pero su timidez desaparece cuando te conoce.
teaching.explanationEs: Shy → shyness con -ness. Her/his + sustantivo.
segments: Mia is shy at first, but her
shyness disappears when she knows you.
teaching.audioText: Mia is shy at first, but her shyness disappears when she knows you.

teaching.en: Tom is an honest student, and his honesty is the reason why we trust him.

teaching.explanationEs: Honest → honesty: el sustantivo termina en -y.
segments: Tom is an honest student, and his honesty

teaching.audioText: Tom is an honest student, and his honesty is the reason why we trust him.

es: Redactar una recomendación breve de una persona para un club o voluntariado usando adjetivos, sustantivos derivados y ejemplos.

teaching.en: I am writing a reference for Mia, who wants to be a volunteer at the animal club.
teaching.es: Escribo una referencia para Mia, que quiere ser voluntaria en el club de animales.
teaching.explanationEs: Write a reference = escribir una carta de recomendación. Volunteer = voluntario.
segments: I am writing a reference for Mia, who wants
to be a volunteer at the animal club.
teaching.audioText: I am writing a reference for Mia, who wants to be a volunteer at the animal club.

teaching.en: Mia is responsible: she always finishes her work, and she takes responsibility when something goes wrong.
teaching.es: Mia es responsable: siempre termina su trabajo y asume la responsabilidad cuando algo sale mal.
teaching.explanationEs: Responsible → responsibility. Take responsibility = asumir la responsabilidad.
segments: Mia is responsible: she always finishes her work,
and she takes responsibility when something goes wrong.
teaching.audioText: Mia is responsible: she always finishes her work, and she takes responsibility when something goes wrong.

teaching.en: She is enthusiastic about every task, and her enthusiasm helps the whole group.

teaching.explanationEs: Enthusiastic about + sustantivo. Enthusiastic → enthusiasm.
segments: She is enthusiastic about every task, and
her enthusiasm helps the whole group.
teaching.audioText: She is enthusiastic about every task, and her enthusiasm helps the whole group.

teaching.en: She is good at teamwork, and she always gives support to new members.

teaching.explanationEs: Give support = dar apoyo. Good at + sustantivo.
segments: She is good at teamwork, and she
always gives support to new members.
teaching.audioText: She is good at teamwork, and she always gives support to new members.

teaching.en: For these reasons, I recommend Mia as a volunteer; I am sure she will be a great help.
teaching.es: Por estas razones, recomiendo a Mia como voluntaria; estoy segura de que será una gran ayuda.
teaching.explanationEs: Recommend + persona + as + función: así se cierra la carta.
segments: For these reasons, I recommend Mia as a volunteer;
I am sure she will be a great help.
teaching.audioText: For these reasons, I recommend Mia as a volunteer; I am sure she will be a great help.

feedback.es: Del adjetivo responsible se pasa al sustantivo responsibility.

prompt.es: Ordena la frase: «Yo la recomiendo como voluntaria.»
